rounds.response:
It’s fine to text short reminders when schedules don’t line up, but save in-person conversations for recurring problems or when you need to reset expectations.  
Keep texts brief, specific, and kind, using an “I” statement and a clear ask/timeframe so it doesn’t feel like a blame note.

Avoid sarcasm, passive-aggressive phrasing, or public notes; a neutral tone (and an emoji only if you normally use them) helps keep it friendly.  
If gentle reminders don’t work, request a short in-person check-in to set a concrete plan (shared calendar, reminders, or agreed consequence) and follow through.
